chunks: If it is said: We object to your statement regarding his Imamate on the basis of his occultation,

We say: If you cannot describe the wisdom of his disappearance, it indicates invalidity of your belief in his Imamate, because if it were valid, you should be able to describe the wisdom of the occultation.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological argument against the Imam's occultation based on the inability to explain its wisdom?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this rationalist objection, which posits that the validity of the Imamate is contingent upon the intelligibility of its divine wisdom (hikmah); thus, the perceived inscrutability of the occultation is treated as a logical disproof. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on reconciling divine decree with human reason, asserting that the occultation is not a defect but a profound, albeit hidden, wisdom that requires deeper contemplation rather than immediate explicit explanation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: If it is said: On the basis of his occultation, we question your belief in his Imamate.

We say: If you cannot describe the wisdom of his disappearance, it indicates invalidity of your belief in his Imamate, because if it were valid, you should be able to describe the wisdom of his occultation.
